workingTitle: A lattice algorithm found a pulsar hidden in sparse gamma rays
publicationStatus: Peer-reviewed Physical Review Letters article published 19 November 2026
coreFacts: PSR J1622-7204 is an isolated gamma-ray pulsar spinning at 261 hertz.
The search used 15 years of Fermi Large Area Telescope data.
The lattice-based method used about ten CPU hours, while a previous semicoherent search failed after roughly 600 CPU years.
Gamma-ray searches are difficult because Fermi typically detects only one photon per roughly 100 million pulsar rotations.
The method maps possible whole-number rotation counts between detected photons onto points in a high-dimensional lattice and searches for short vectors.

sources.label: Gamma-Ray Pulsar Discovery Using a Lattice-Based Method

sourceStatus: Peer-reviewed Physical Review Letters paper and the authors' institute release were read and agree on the measured result.
caveats: The study demonstrates one discovery; the claim that the method could uncover many more pulsars, especially binaries, is a prospective inference.
The short runtime in the successful search benefited from luck: the team reports that 300 runs would be needed for a 95 percent success probability.
